choices: That suspense requires showing the bomb
That scenes must turn on a value
That we impose a beginning and an end on mere sequence, so the interval means something
questions.explain: A plot is an extended tick-tock: organized time between a humble genesis and a feeble apocalypse.

questions.q: Which pair describes chronos and kairos?
choices: Passing time, and time charged with meaning by its relation to an end

questions.q: Test audiences say they saw the ending coming from the first act. What does Kermode's account of peripeteia suggest?
choices: Keep the destination but reach it by a route that falsifies their simple expectations
questions.explain: We want the end, but by an unexpected road, still arriving at concord.

questions.q: What does Brooks mean by the 'anticipation of retrospection'?
choices: We read forward expecting the end to let us look back and understand
questions.explain: For Brooks, the end gives meaning to the middle.

questions.q: A thriller resolves its central conflict at the midpoint and coasts to the end. What would Brooks call this?
choices: A short circuit: reaching the end before the middle has worked through the story's energy
questions.explain: The middle is a necessary detour; resolving too early discharges energy cheaply.

questions.q: Which work of Freud's does Brooks use as a model of plot?
questions.explain: He reads its account of organisms returning to rest by their own path as a masterplot.

questions.q: What was Susan Winnett's objection to Brooks?
choices: That his model of arousal and discharge mirrors male experience and presents it as universal
That he relied on Russian formalism
That he wrote only about poetry
questions.explain: In 'Coming Unstrung' (PMLA, 1990) she asked what a plot theory starting from women's experience would look like.

questions.q: Why does Kermode warn about fictions becoming myths?
choices: A fiction taken as literal truth about the world can become dangerous, as in apocalyptic politics
Myths are older and less sophisticated
Fiction should never deal with history
questions.explain: Good fictions are held knowingly, as tools for making sense of time.

ideas: Tick is a humble genesis, tock a feeble apocalypse: plot turns mere duration into meaningful time.
We are born and die in the middle of things, so we make fictions that give the middle a beginning and end.
Reading is driven by the anticipation of retrospection: we read forward to the moment we can look back.
A story's middle is a detour that delays the end, and reaching the end too soon is a short circuit.
